# runelay

> runelay is an open-source, self-hosted MCP gateway. It gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok and any MCP client the same connected accounts, skills and shared memory through one endpoint (`/v1/mcp`). It runs as a desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) or as one Docker container with SQLite. MIT licensed, free, no third-party cloud.

## Get started

- [Download the desktop app](https://runelay.com/download/): Mac (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux AppImage. Runs the server on `127.0.0.1:4312`.
- [Set up step by step](https://runelay.com/setup/): install the server with `curl -fsSL runelay.com/install | sh`, then the CLI with `curl -fsSL runelay.com/cli | sh`, then `runelay login`, `runelay migrate` and `runelay connect`.
- [Agent setup prompt](https://runelay.com/setup/): a ready prompt that lets an agent install and connect runelay for you.

## Benchmark

- [runelay vs Executor, measured](https://runelay.com/benchmark/): same 11 MCP servers (125 tools), self-hosted Docker. runelay uses 1,045 context tokens at connect vs 2,729, tool calls are 10x faster (6.6 ms vs 68 ms median), search is 60x faster, idle RAM is 8.4x lower. Since runelay 0.3.3 the Docker image is a 66 MB download vs 80 MB for Executor.

## Guides

- [Self-hosted MCP gateway, the practical guide](https://runelay.com/self-hosted-mcp-gateway/): what an MCP gateway does, why self-host it, what to check before picking one and how to run runelay in a minute.
- [Open-source, self-hosted Composio alternative](https://runelay.com/composio-alternative/): runelay vs Composio side by side, when each one fits and how to switch with `runelay migrate`.
- [MCP gateway vs MCP server](https://runelay.com/mcp-gateway-vs-mcp-server/): the difference in context cost, credentials, revocation and audit, and when you need a gateway.

## MCP tools

- `list_connections`, `search_tools`, `call_tool`, `execute`: find and call tools from every connected account; `execute` chains calls in a sandboxed JavaScript runtime.
- `search_context`, `read_memory`, `write_memory`, `read_skill`, `read_skill_file`: shared memory and skills across agents.
